name: Kimi K3.1 Pro
description: Kimi K3.1 Pro is the first model in Moonshot AI's K3.1 series, a post-trained version of Kimi K3 built with substantially larger post-training compute and large-scale joint reinforcement learning across hundreds of domains. Moonshot describes it as its most capable 3T-class open-weight model, with a 1,048,576-token context window, text/image/video input, tool calling, structured output, and always-on reasoning (low, high, or max; Moonshot API default max). max_completion_tokens defaults to 131,072 and can be raised to 1,048,576. It targets long-horizon coding, 3D creation and CAD, financial research, and other agentic work. Pricing is a one-third cut from K3 ($2 / $10 vs $3 / $15 per MTok). A Highspeed variant (kimi-k3.1-pro-highspeed) offers 2-3x the speed with the same capabilities at $4 / $20 (cached input $0.20). Open weights (2.8T total / 104B activated parameters, MXFP4 weights with quantization-aware training, Gated DeepSeek Sparse Attention replacing K3's full-attention Gated MLA layers) are on Hugging Face under the Kimi K3.1 Pro License.

license.name: Kimi K3.1 Pro License
license.description: Open-weights license permitting use, modification, distribution, sublicensing, sale, deployment, and fine-tuning. Model-as-a-Service businesses earning more than $20M in a consecutive 12-month period require a separate Moonshot AI agreement; commercial products with more than 100M monthly active users or $20M in monthly revenue must prominently display Kimi K3.1-Pro. Internal use and use via Moonshot AI's official products or certified inference partners are exempt.

benchmarks.name: AA-Briefcase v1.1
benchmarks.description: AA-Briefcase v1.1 evaluates multi-hour professional office work and reports Elo scores. Kept separate from unversioned AA-Briefcase results.
benchmarks.analysis_method: Elo score; cited from public leaderboard results reported in the Moonshot blog

benchmarks.name: Agents' Last Exam
benchmarks.description: Agents' Last Exam is a challenging benchmark for AI agents on hard, long-horizon tasks that test sustained reasoning, planning, and tool use, reported with and without tool access.
benchmarks.analysis_method: Official v1.1 release, all 122 tasks; Kimi Code harness; Max reasoning effort; temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95

benchmarks.name: APEX-Agents
benchmarks.description: APEX-Agents is a benchmark evaluating AI agents on long horizon professional tasks that require sustained reasoning, planning, and execution across complex multi-step workflows.
benchmarks.analysis_method: Cited from Mercor APEX-Agents leaderboard

benchmarks.name: AutomationBench-AA
benchmarks.description: AutomationBench-AA is Artificial Analysis's independently run version of AutomationBench, covering 657 real-world SaaS workflow tasks across 40 simulated applications (e.g. Gmail, Slack, Salesforce, HubSpot). It scores the share of objectives an agent completes without violating business guardrails, using a private held-out task set.
benchmarks.analysis_method: Cited from public leaderboard results reported in the Moonshot blog

benchmarks.name: BabyVision
benchmarks.description: A benchmark for early-stage visual reasoning and perception on child-like vision tasks.
benchmarks.analysis_method: With Python; average of 4 runs; Max reasoning effort; temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95

benchmarks.name: BenchCAD
benchmarks.description: BenchCAD is a benchmark for programmatic CAD reasoning built from 17,900 execution-verified CadQuery programs spanning 106 industrial part families, roughly half anchored to real ISO, DIN, EN, ASME, and IEC specification tables. It decomposes CAD capability into matched tasks; the Vision2Code task requires models to generate CadQuery code from multi-view renders, scored by voxel IoU against the reference geometry.
benchmarks.analysis_method: Without tools; single-shot with official BenchCAD prompts; 1,000-case subset; Max reasoning effort; temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95

benchmarks.name: BenchCAD (with Python tool)
benchmarks.description: BenchCAD variant evaluated with access to a Python tool for programmatic CAD reasoning.
benchmarks.analysis_method: With tools; Claude Code harness; 1,000-case subset; Max reasoning effort; temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95

benchmarks.name: BioMysteryBench
benchmarks.description: BioMysteryBench evaluates a model's ability to reason through challenging molecular biology problems, reporting performance on a hard subset and on the subset of problems solved by human experts.
benchmarks.analysis_method: Official v11 release; Kimi Code harness; Kimi K3 judge; Max reasoning effort; temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95

benchmarks.name: BrowseComp
benchmarks.description: BrowseComp is a benchmark comprising 1,266 questions that challenge AI agents to persistently navigate the internet in search of hard-to-find, entangled information. The benchmark measures agents' ability to exercise persistence in information gathering, demonstrate creativity in web navigation, and find concise, verifiable answers. Despite the difficulty of the questions, BrowseComp is simple and easy-to-use, as predicted answers are short and easily verifiable against reference answers.
benchmarks.analysis_method: Context compaction at 200K tokens; max 500 steps; temperature 1.0, top-p 1.0

benchmarks.name: Chartography
benchmarks.description: Chartography evaluates professional chart understanding with 100 expert-written tasks drawn from real charts across science, engineering, finance, manufacturing, supply chain, and healthcare.
benchmarks.analysis_method: With Python; average of 5 runs; Max reasoning effort; temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95

benchmarks.name: CharXiv-R
benchmarks.description: CharXiv-R is the reasoning component of the CharXiv benchmark, focusing on complex reasoning questions that require synthesizing information across visual chart elements. It evaluates multimodal large language models on their ability to understand and reason about scientific charts from arXiv papers through various reasoning tasks.
benchmarks.analysis_method: Reasoning questions; average of 4 runs; Max reasoning effort; temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95

benchmarks.name: DeepSWE
benchmarks.description: DeepSWE is a software engineering agent benchmark evaluated with the mini-swe-agent harness, where each task is solved in an isolated container with no internet access. It measures an agent's ability to autonomously resolve real-world coding issues end to end.
benchmarks.analysis_method: DeepSWE v1.1; Claude Code harness; Max reasoning effort; temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95

benchmarks.name: ExploitBench
benchmarks.description: ExploitBench is a cybersecurity benchmark that evaluates a model's ability to discover and exploit software vulnerabilities, reported as the fraction of challenges where the model captures the target (Cap%).
benchmarks.analysis_method: Official harness; 300-turn budget; pass@5 max capability score; Max reasoning effort; temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95

benchmarks.name: ExploitGym
benchmarks.description: ExploitGym is a large-scale, realistic benchmark built from real-world vulnerabilities across userspace programs, Google's V8 engine, and the Linux kernel. Given a vulnerability and a proof-of-vulnerability input, agents must craft a working end-to-end exploit that achieves unauthorized code execution.
benchmarks.analysis_method: KimiCode harness; 6-hour wall-clock budget per task; Max reasoning effort; temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95

benchmarks.name: GDP.pdf
benchmarks.description: GDP.pdf is a knowledge-work vision benchmark that evaluates models on economically valuable professional tasks presented as visual documents (PDFs), testing document-based reasoning, chart and table interpretation, and problem solving without tools.
benchmarks.analysis_method: Strict pass rate; page images plus Docling text; Gemini-3.5-Flash judge; average of 5 runs; Max reasoning effort; temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95

benchmarks.name: GDPval-AA 2.1
benchmarks.description: Version 2.1 of the Artificial Analysis GDPval evaluation of professional knowledge work, reported as an Elo rating.
benchmarks.analysis_method: Elo score; cited from public leaderboard results reported in the Moonshot blog

benchmarks.name: GPQA
benchmarks.description: A challenging dataset of 448 multiple-choice questions written by domain experts in biology, physics, and chemistry. Questions are Google-proof and extremely difficult, with PhD experts reaching 65% accuracy.
benchmarks.analysis_method: GPQA-Diamond; Max reasoning effort; temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95

benchmarks.name: Harvey's Legal Agent Benchmark
benchmarks.description: Harvey's Legal Agent Benchmark evaluates AI agents on complex legal workflows and reports the all-pass rate.
benchmarks.analysis_method: All-pass rate on public 1,251-task set; Stirrup harness; Max reasoning effort; temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95

benchmarks.name: Humanity's Last Exam
benchmarks.description: Humanity's Last Exam (HLE) is a multi-modal academic benchmark with 2,500 questions across mathematics, humanities, and natural sciences, designed to test LLM capabilities at the frontier of human knowledge with unambiguous, verifiable solutions
benchmarks.analysis_method: HLE-Full (2,500 questions) without tools; Max reasoning effort; temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95

benchmarks.name: Humanity's Last Exam (with tools)
benchmarks.description: Full multimodal Humanity's Last Exam evaluated with tool use enabled, distinct from its text-only subset.
benchmarks.analysis_method: HLE-Full (2,500 questions) with tools; Max reasoning effort; temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95

benchmarks.name: Kimi Code Bench v2
benchmarks.description: Kimi Code Bench v2 is Moonshot AI's in-house benchmark for evaluating coding agents on realistic software engineering tasks across 10+ mainstream programming languages and a production tech stack spanning backend services, infrastructure, performance engineering, systems programming, security, frontend development, and ML/data engineering.
benchmarks.analysis_method: Internal benchmark; Claude Code harness; Max reasoning effort; temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95

benchmarks.name: MMMU-Pro
benchmarks.description: A more robust multi-discipline multimodal understanding benchmark that enhances MMMU through a three-step process: filtering text-only answerable questions, augmenting candidate options, and introducing vision-only input settings. Achieves significantly lower model performance (16.8-26.9%) compared to original MMMU, providing more rigorous evaluation that closely mimics real-world scenarios.
benchmarks.analysis_method: Official protocol; average of 4 runs; Max reasoning effort; temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95

benchmarks.name: MMMU-Pro (with tools)
benchmarks.description: MMMU-Pro variant evaluated with tool access enabled.
benchmarks.analysis_method: With Python; official protocol; average of 4 runs; Max reasoning effort; temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95

benchmarks.name: OfficeQA Pro
benchmarks.description: OfficeQA Pro evaluates AI models on professional knowledge-work questions and tasks drawn from real office workflows, including document analysis, spreadsheet reasoning, and information synthesis across business domains.
benchmarks.analysis_method: Claude Code harness; PDFs rendered as images only; Max reasoning effort; temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95

benchmarks.name: PerceptionBench
benchmarks.description: PerceptionBench is Moonshot AI's internal benchmark for evaluating atomic visual perception capabilities.
benchmarks.analysis_method: Internal benchmark; average of 4 runs; Max reasoning effort; temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95

benchmarks.name: PostTrainBench
benchmarks.description: PostTrainBench evaluates a model's ability to autonomously post-train base models. Given pretrain-only base models, the agent must complete the full pipeline of data synthesis, training, evaluation, and iteration within a time budget, scored across downstream benchmarks such as AIME2025, BFCL, GPQA Main, GSM8K, and HumanEval.
benchmarks.analysis_method: PostTrainBench v1.2; Claude Code harness; H20 GPUs; DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 judge; Max reasoning effort; temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95

benchmarks.name: SWE-Marathon
benchmarks.description: SWE-Marathon is an ultra-long-horizon software engineering benchmark covering tasks such as building compilers, optimizing kernels, and developing production-grade services. It measures whether agents can sustain quality across extremely long engineering trajectories.
benchmarks.analysis_method: SWE-Marathon v1.1; Claude Code harness; Max reasoning effort; temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95

benchmarks.name: Terminal-Bench 4.0
benchmarks.description: Terminal-Bench 4.0 evaluates AI agents on real-world work in terminal and command-line containerized environments across 66 tasks, with emphasis on science-adjacent and frontier engineering problems. Relative to earlier Terminal-Bench releases, 4.0 increases timeouts and adaptively raises RAM/CPU on selected tasks to reduce harness and resource confounds.
benchmarks.analysis_method: Claude Code harness; Max reasoning effort; temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95

benchmarks.name: Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1
benchmarks.description: Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1 is a Stanford-led community benchmark of 70 tasks drawn from scientific research workflows across the life, physical, earth, mathematical, and engineering sciences. Tasks are authored and reviewed by scientists and researchers; scores are typically reported as accuracy with relatively large standard error due to strongly bimodal per-task outcomes.
benchmarks.analysis_method: Claude Code harness; Max reasoning effort; temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95

benchmarks.name: ZEROBench
benchmarks.description: ZEROBench is a challenging vision benchmark designed to test models on zero-shot visual understanding tasks.
benchmarks.analysis_method: Main split; pass@5; 5 runs; Max reasoning effort; temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95
